subject: PrivPool watchband sizing & mix-mode scaling review
messages:
From: Mike Tang <mike@greenway.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial capacity request: private GPU pool for Greenway inference

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks for taking this. A quick summary of what Greenway needs for their private (VPC) deployment so we can get a sizing proposal in front of procurement:

- Workload: clinical summarization + structured extraction (many short prompts).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~2.2M tokens/day (~25 TPS average).
- Peak short-window QPS: up to 1,100 concurrent requests during morning rush (bursty, 5–10 minute windows).
- Latency target: 95th < 200ms for text gen baseline; 99th < 400ms ideally.
- Median prompt length: ~40 tokens; 99p token-length ~1,200.
- Compliance: EU region, private VPC, strict egress control.
- Budget guidance: procurement wants an estimate for a 12-month reserved posture and an ops playbook for handling spikes.

Attached is a short brief with their internal traffic sample and retention constraints (greenway_capacity_request.pdf). Can you sketch a sizing + scaling approach and propose a canary plan?

Best,
Mike Tang
Head of Platform — Greenway Systems

(Attachment: greenway_capacity_request.pdf)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Mike Tang <mike@greenway.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-08T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial capacity request: private GPU pool for Greenway inference

Mike — thanks for the brief and the sample traces. Looping in our infra and capacity leads (David, Mina, Hannah).

High level: Greenway's pattern is a classic steady+spike workload. Rather than pure overprovisioning, we recommend a watchband approach: a steady "baseline band" of capacity sized for sustained throughput and a narrow "burst band" that can spin up quickly for short windows. This reduces unit cost while still meeting your 99th/95th latency goals.

Can you confirm two quick items so our sizing math is accurate:
- Are the 1,100 concurrent requests typically uniform (many short requests) or a small number of very long requests?
- Any hard upper limit on monthly egress / traffic leaving Greenway's VPC?

I'll attach an initial proposal workbook with a few watchband configurations and a rough canary checklist (privpool_proposal_v1.xlsx). Would you be available for a 45-min sizing sync Thursday?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: privpool_proposal_v1.xlsx)

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mike@greenway.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-09T08:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial capacity request: private GPU pool for Greenway inference — rough sizing + test artifacts

Olga / team / Mike — did a quick pass on the sample traces and sketched three candidate watchband ladders. High-level notes and numbers below; I've attached a tiny PoC trace summary from our lab run (watchband_test_results-0509.json).

Summary recommendations (ballpark, pre-POC):
- Baseline Band (sustained): 4 x A100-equivalent nodes (assume model pinned to 16k context, 8-bit quantized variant). This maps to ~100 sustained QPS with 95th latency ~120ms given caching of recent prefixes.
- Burst Band (fast spin-up): +6 nodes (warm pool nodes that can be promoted within 30–60s via container spin-up + KV-cache prewarm hooks) — absorbs short 5–10 minute windows, pushing peak QPS capacity to ~700–900 depending on model variant and batching.
- Long-tail Shock: maintain a secondary fallback routing to a slightly larger hosted variant (if allowed) for multi-minute sustained surges beyond the burst band.

Network / NIC guidance:
- Dedicated subnet, NIC sizing: minimum 100Gbps per host for headroom (packetized gen + embeddings). Oversubscribe NICs no more than 1.5x if using multi-tenant appliance.
- Egress cordon: enforce per-tenant egress caps at the VPC egress gateway — Greenway should set a soft alarm at 60% of monthly allowance.

SLO / autoscaling ops:
- Autoscaler should use request-concurrency + observed token-per-second metrics in the admission controller.
- Warmup window: prewarm KV caches for known prefixes (recommended 90s warmup for clinical models).

Next steps: 1) Confirm token medians & 99p lengths (Mike) — these materially affect nodes in the burst band, 2) agree on canary date, 3) define fallback route (hosted vs larger private pool).

Reference: JIRA INFRA-9743 captures our canary infra changes.

-David
David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: watchband_test_results-0509.json)

From: Mike Tang <mike@greenway.com>

Subject: Re: Initial capacity request: private GPU pool for Greenway inference — questions

Thanks David — quick clarifications below:

- Concurrency profile: ~90% of requests are short (<150 tokens) single-shot prompts; the remaining 10% are longer interactive sessions that can last up to a minute but are far less frequent. So the heavy tail is token-length-driven, not concurrency.
- Egress ceiling: procurement set a hard cap of 12 TB/mo. We can negotiate higher but need to model costs under 12TB.
- Isolation: canary must not share model KV caches with other tenants; Greenway needs dedicated cache lanes.

Can you validate the baseline band above if we pin to a 4-bit quantized variant (we expect slightly different perf numbers)? Also, what does promotion from warm pool to active look like in terms of time and expected cold-latency spike?

-Mike

Date: 2029-05-10T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial capacity request — networking & ops constraints

+1 on David's recommendations. A few network/ops specifics to lock down for the canary and production:

- Dedicated subnet + egress NAT: place Greenway in a private subnet with a dedicated egress NAT appliance so we can enforce the 12TB cap centrally.
- Cross-AZ placement: distribute baseline band across 2 AZs to reduce blast radius; place burst band in same AZs to keep intra-AZ traffic low-latency.
- Firewall rules: only allow outbound to Greenway's approved endpoints (for telemetry + S3 destinations).
- Cache isolation: implement per-tenant KV namespaces; warm nodes prepopulate top 5k patient prefixes during promotion. This reduces cold spike magnitude.
- Admission control thresholds: set token-p-s based cutoff that triggers promotion; also include "burst dampers" — short-term request shaper that smooths immediate peaks if promotion latency is exceeded.

Action items before canary:
1) Finalize NIC sizing and confirm 100Gbps host plan.
2) Confirm model quantization variant and pin (Mike).
3) Bake prewarm job and run 2h soak with production traces (we can run next Tue in staging).

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Infrastructure Lead — Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: PrivPool watchband sizing & next steps (canary plan)

Mike — wrapping up the thread with a concise mutual action plan and recommended sizing so procurement and SRE have something to review.

Mutual action plan (agreed items):
- Sizing: baseline 4 x A100-equivalent nodes (16k context, 4-bit quantized model variant) + burst band 6 nodes (warm pool) — targets: 95th latency ~130ms, 99th for short prompts <350ms with KV prewarm.
- Network: 100Gbps NIC per host, dedicated egress NAT with 12TB/mo soft alarm at 60% threshold. Cross-AZ baseline placement.
- Isolation: per-tenant KV namespaces and dedicated subnet for canary; no shared cache lanes.
- Canary schedule: staging soak on 2029-05-14 (2h), production canary on 2029-05-20 (3-day observation window).
- Fallback: route >3m sustained tokens/day or >15 min sustained above burst threshold to a hosted fallback endpoint (policy-defined) — we'll supply a policy template.

Deliverables from Redwood:
1) Finalized workbook with cost and capacity curves (updated after you confirm 4-bit perf numbers).
2) Canary runbook + JIRA INFRA-9743 ticket with run steps and rollback criteria.
3) Test artifacts and the PoC summary (attached).

Please confirm the canary timeline and whether procurement can accept the baseline + burst band recommendation for the committed contract. If we get confirmation, we'll follow up with a short invite for a kickoff and handoff to SRE to start the staging soak.

Thanks — excited to help Greenway get this deployed with predictable economics.
